label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their mean scores on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale, PHQ-9 depression scale, and GAD-7 anxiety scale are all notably higher than typical thresholds, with anxiety symptoms being particularly pronounced. This cluster of 140 respondents suggests a pattern in which heavy digital engagement co-occurs with significant psychological distress across multiple dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media usage averaging approximately 3.9 hours with a substantial proportion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.78) indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Higher depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.81) suggesting moderate depressive tendencies
Notably high anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.27), the most pronounced distress indicator in this profile
Co-occurrence of multiple psychological distress markers alongside intensive social-media engagement

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their daily social media use is relatively light, averaging roughly 2.8 hours per day (within the 1–3 hour bracket). Across all psychological well-being indicators, this group scores well below scale midpoints, suggesting generally positive mental health and moderate digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social media consumption averaging approximately 2.8 hours
Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78, well below scale midpoint)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27)
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03)
Pattern consistent with balanced digital habits and strong psychosocial functioning

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who report elevated loneliness yet comparatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms, despite spending nearly five hours per day on social media. Their loneliness scores stand above average while their PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores remain modest, suggesting that heavy social-media engagement may coexist with emotional isolation without necessarily escalating into clinical-level mood or anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, approximately 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Heavier daily social-media use averaging close to 5 hours per day
Elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) relative to other profiles
Below-average depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90)
Below-average anxiety symptom severity (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85)
Sustained high screen-time engagement despite feelings of social disconnection
tone: Socially disconnected yet psychologically stable; quietly isolated rather than overtly distressed

label: Well-Adjusted Graduate Male with Light Social-Media Use
summary: This profile represents a group of 217 respondents characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, combined with relatively light daily social-media use averaging roughly 1.6 hours. Their mean scores on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale (1.22), PHQ-9 depression scale (0.82), and GAD-7 anxiety scale (0.90) all fall well below clinical concern thresholds, suggesting generally positive psychological well-being. These individuals tend to be highly educated males who maintain a moderate and bounded relationship with social media.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media use averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Low self-reported loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ~1.22)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ~0.82)
Minimal anxiety symptomatology (GAD-7 mean ~0.90)
Social-media engagement kept within a bounded 1–3 hour daily window
